cd /home/nab-raj.roshyara@dg-nexolution.de/roshyara/personal/nrna1/docs/knowledgeos/knowlegeos_manual_theory_20261018/06-theory/manuscript; python3 -I - <<'EOF'
p='chapter_01/CH-01-knowledge-authority-execution.md'; s=open(p).read()
R=[
("- **another decision first**: two root questions block 11 others;",
 "- **another decision first**: two root questions. The register counts 11 items blocked by them, but four of those are not questions (a technology stack, gates, field lists, row statuses), so the roots block **7** questions [DR L86–105];"),
("These are four kinds of **prerequisite**. In the register, the **closing step itself is always an act**.",
 "These are four kinds of **prerequisite**, and they can combine. Some questions need **all** of several (one waits on two decisions [DR L103, L105]); others need **any one** of several (\"a second lineage **or** external review\" [DR L123]). In the register, the **closing step itself is always an act**."),
("- *Open (different question types):* for a **decision question** (what the organisation will do or adopt), closure is an act. For a **factual or research question**, evidence can *answer* it, but recording that answer as accepted is still an act, because it changes standing. Whether some factual questions may be treated as closed by evidence alone, without an act, is not settled here;",
 "- *Two closure rules, by kind of question (Ded; supported by the register's own examples):*\n  - a **decision question** (what the organisation will do or adopt) closes by a **valid act** alone, once its prerequisites are met;\n  - a **factual or research question** (e.g. \"is the link verified?\" [DR L122]) closes only by **evidence meeting the standard of its kind** (§1.16.8), **recorded** by an act. No act can make it true; the act records that the evidence meets the standard.\n\n  Whether some factual questions may be treated as closed by evidence without any recording act is not settled here;"),
("Supersession as a link (I-7) makes pinning cheap: old versions persist, so *d*@*v* stays resolvable.",
 "Supersession as a link (I-7) makes pinning cheap: old versions persist, so *d*@*v* stays resolvable.\n\n**Pinning applies to the deciding logic too, and to identities (Src: PC L67–69; DE L364–368).** A decision is reconstructable only if **both** its inputs **and the version of the logic that decided** are recorded: \"a policy whose rules changed silently makes every prior decision unexplainable\" [PC L67]. The same discipline gives idempotency: \"identity must include the version of what was read\" [DE L368]."),
]
for a,b in R:
    assert s.count(a)==1,a[:60]; s=s.replace(a,b)
open(p,'w').write(s); print('ok')
EOF
